title: I had a game idea and prototype in 2023 and never finished it. I picked it back up with Claude Opus 5.5 and turned it into a real game: Gunhop (free, playable in the itch.io)
author: Asyte
selftext:
Back in 2023 I made a small prototype of an idea I'd had for a while, which is to propel yourself with your shots and kill enemies while maneuvering in the air like that. Something like, Downwell, but upwards. You climb a vertical shaft by shooting, and every shot kicks you away from where you aim. Your ammo is also your fuel. The prototype worked, sort of, and then it sat in a folder for three years as quite a lot of my other projects.

A few days ago, I opened it again with Claude Opus 5.5 to see how far we could take it. What came out is pretty much the game I had in my head in 2023, but a lot better, as it seems Opus 5.5 knows ball.(for game dev at least)

Stack

Godot 4.6 with GDScript, exported to the web for itch.io. Claude Code with Opus 5.5 as the lead. It splits the work across parallel Sonnet agents, reviews their code and screenshots, and merges it. I direct the feel and the look: what's fun, what feels off, what I want next. Hero and enemy sprites start as Gemini concept sheets, which get converted to pixel art. Everything else is drawn in code, and all the sound is made in code.

Recoil movement tuned until it felt weighty but controllable. Hit-stop, screen shake and a proper crosshair. Generated shafts built from hand-made chunks. The gaps grow as your upgrades make you more agile. 4 levels × 4 shafts (Crypt, Ice, Machinery, Core), each with its own look, enemies and ambient sound. A boss at the top of every level, with an intro and a sleeping pose until you wake it. Gold, upgrade cards, a shop and 4 guns (pistol, full-auto SMG, shotgun, rail gun). A short intro cinematic for game start.

What I believe helped for the development:

Every system has automated tests: 41 suites, run headless.

A playtest bot plays the whole run to check that every shaft can be climbed and that the difficulty feels fair.

A roadmap document plus a Trello board, and a phase-by-phase workflow. I play each build and send notes; the next build fixes them.

I really value the feedback some friends have given me on the game's general feel and suggestions on what can be added on it.
